title: Knights of the Shield Hideout
html:

Elfsong Tavern
The Knights of the Shield Hideout is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3.
“
My old home - thank you for bringing me back. Look around - you'll find some of my things still intact. Perhaps even useful to you.
„
— Emperor, upon entering its old lodgings

Overview

The Knights of the Shield Hideout is a secret part of the Elfsong Tavern basement, which in the recent past served as the headquarters of a secret society known as the  Knights of the Shield. This organization, based in Baldur's Gate, operated in information dealing, political manipulation, and smuggling.

For a certain period of time the organization was run by the  Emperor and  Duke Belynne Stelmane. The society's customer-facing operations were conducted in Duke Stelmane's private parlour on the first floor of the Elfsong Tavern. When  Enver Gortash set out for his quest for power over Baldur's Gate, the Knights of the Shield became his prime target.[1] Eventually, Gortash discovered the Emperor's presence behind the organization and, having his main plan in progress, betrayed it to the Elder Brain. Soon after, the Knights' influence dwindled to a nigh,[2] and its headquarters was abandoned.

Access

The Knight of the Shield Hideout can be accessed from two points:

  • From the Elfsong Tavern Basement, a hidden button is located at X: -868 Y: 544 within a side room. Pressing it opens a wine barrel in another room with a hidden hallway and stairs leading down to the Knights of the Shield Hideout.
  • Alternatively, the hideout can be accessed from the sewers via a ladder located at X: 52 Y: 793. This brings the party to the hidden room directly.

Elfsong Tavern basement

A stairway from the Elfsong Tavern kitchen leads down to the basement. In the main area no less than 30  rats skitter about, as part of the ⁠Roveer's Storehouse quest. They are hostile on sight, and must be eliminated to move further.

In the back are two separate rooms. The larger one in the center is filled with large wine barrels, while the smaller one on the side is filled with wine racks. The cellar can be looted for a number of Camp Supplies, mostly various types of wine.

Inside the smaller room at X: -868 Y: 544 is a hidden button, highlighted with a  DC 0 Perception Check. Pressing it opens the head of a wine barrel in the larger room like a door, revealing a hidden hallway with stairs leading down to the Knights of the Shield Hideout.[3]

Main Hall of the Hideout

Entering the location via the Elfsong Tavern leads the party to the main room. An antechamber ends with a short stairway, which is divided in two by a small ground with balusters.

In the center a is large round table, presumably where the knights met.[4] On the sides are two higher areas, only accessible via the stairs in the far part of the room.

Several containers and items of interest are around the room:

  • A Heavy chest at X: -723 Y: 546 contains gold, a random gem, and a  Potion of Superior Healing
  • A  Silver Key on the desk at X: -728 Y: 540 opens the door from the Hidden Room to the Lower City Sewers (if needed, see Involvement subsection below)
  • Several display cases contain random Valuables
  • The  Hhune Mausoleum Key is in a Mahogany Wardrobe along with two random sets of high-grade Camp Clothing
  • On the desk near the wardrobe is a map titled  Location of Reserve Supplies, which mentions two points of buried treasure, though no markers are added on the map after reading it[verify]

Involvement

When the party approach the Elfsong Tavern from the Lower City streets for the first time, the Emperor chimes in, drawing their attention to the establishment. It tells the party about its old dwelling hidden somewhere inside, thus starting the ⁠Visit the Emperor's Old Hideout quest.

Inside the hideout proper, a group of Githyanki are waiting for the party. They act on orders of  Vlaakith and are looking for the  Astral Prism. If a party member has the  Qua'nith Psionic Detector in their inventory, it alerts them, and they comment on it. The particular comment depends on the circumstances of how the detector was obtained.

The party can also explore the hideout, coming from the Lower City Sewers through the door at X: 40 Y: 800. In this case, the cutscene with Orin shapeshifted as a kidnapped companion triggers (if this event has not happened prior). The door is locked (requires the  Silver Key found in the Main Hall or  DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check), but if Orin appears, she opens the door herself. The Emperor's quest starts after passing the doorway, though its notions differ. In this case, the party first enter the Hidden Room (see below) and can explore it. However, the Qua'nith detector does not trigger in this room, and the only warning the party get comes from the Emperor – when they approach the movable wall section.

By default, the githyanki squad is led by  Ch'r'ai Har'rak. However, if  Ch'r'ai W'wargaz and / or  Ch'r'ai Tska'an were not defeated by the party in previous Acts of the game, one or both of them are also present. On both higher areas are two Gate Masters,  Ri'zel and  Zyrlak, who are holding open  Astral Rifts to summon reinforcements in a possible fight.

The githyanki can be snuck up on or conversed with. If  Lae'zel is present, a successful  DC 18 Intimidation or Persuasion Check results in them leaving peacefully; this also gains approval from  +1. If Lae'zel is not present, or if the roll is failed, a fight is inevitable.

During the fight, the Gate Masters do not directly participate. Each turn, one of the two summons a new Veteran Warrior or Veteran Raider, who join the battle on their next turn. The rift disappears when the Gate Master holding it is defeated, loses concentration on the spell, or once three reinforcements have been summoned through this gate. If the Gate Master is still alive when their rift closes, they join the battle.

Hidden Room

On the far North wall, behind a large knight statue, on the right side of an indent is a hidden button at X: -734 Y: 577 which can be seen with a  DC 0 Perception Check.[5] Using the button reveals a hidden doorway, behind which is  the Emperor's old room, where it kept many mementos of its former life. Most are are highlighted with  DC 0 Perception Checks. Some of these items can be taken and used.

Interacting with the  Sword of the Emperor successfully completes the quest ⁠Visit the Emperor's Old Hideout, even if other items are left in the room. Completing the quest, however, does not deactivate the Emperor's possible comments on unexplored points of interest; the party can still learn about them later. Three stone bookcases in the corners of the room contain a random spell scroll each, up to Very rare grade.

The door at X: -745 Y: 590 lead to a lesser room with a hatch which, in turn, leads to the sewers. Containers on the shelves around this room contain nothing significant.

Below the hatch a small storeroom. Numerous Traveller's Chests on the shelves at X: 56 Y: 796, as well as Wooden Chest in the opposite corner, contain gold, random Valuables, potions and / or spell scrolls up to Very rare grade. In the southwestern corner is a table with a journal describing Duke Stelmane's ongoing illness before her murder. The Stack of Books near the table contains two books concerning Mind Flayers, and on the bench nearby is a  Scroll of Detect Thoughts.

The Emperor's special items

These are the items found in the hidden room. The Emperor has ambient commentary on each of the items, if interacted with.

Special item Location The Emperor's commentary
Butter Fork X: -731 Y: 596 "My cutlery set - a gift from my mother. The butter knife is missing, but otherwise it looks to be complete. I don't need it anymore, but the memory stirs something in me still."[6]
Chains X: -739 Y: 594 "The chains I used to bind my meals - villains and lawbreakers. You see I tried to exercise morality, where I could."
 Dog Collar X: -742 Y: 584 "Rascal's collar...My poor four-legged friend. Their lives are so brief, so simple, and yet - full."[7][8]
Emperor's Wardrobe X: -727 Y: 590 "My old wardrobe - the home of all my disguises. We are what we appear to be, and so appearances matter."
Empty Brain Jar X: -745 Y: 593 "An old container for brains. Empty - shame. It would have been nice to find one to sustain me now."
 Recipe for Fiddlehead Soup X: -744 Y: 587 "A recipe for fiddlehead soup - a favourite meal of mine, when I had need of meals like that."[9]
Stelmane's Portrait X: -732 Y: 597 "There she is in all her glory - Duke Belynne Stelmane. My old partner."[10]
 Sword of the Emperor X: -734 Y: 589 "My old sword - my first purchase as an adventurer. No use to me anymore. It's yours, if you want it."[8]
Unique Shell X: -726 Y: 586 "A shell - a keepsake from my final voyage. Pinched in a moment of sentimentality."

Notes and references

  1. ↑ As stated in  Inroads by Arms Dealer Gortash and  For Duke Stelmane.
  2. ↑ As stated in  Enhanced' Weapons - Sales Ledger.
  3. ↑ A responding button on the wall at X: -862 Y: 554 can be used if the hideout is entered from the sewers. It is in plain sight and does not require an ability check.
  4. ↑ Though no former members of the organisation are encountered in the game, its name and the image of the round table may imply certain tropes of the legend of King Arthur and his knights.
  5. ↑ A corresponding button exists on the opposite side of the wall to open the movable section from within. Characters often pass the check for both buttons simultaneously through the closed door, so it may appear as if they passed the check twice.
  6. ↑ The name of the item is "Butter Fork", implicitly because of the "missing" butter knife. As  Balduran#LegacyForgotten Realms lore claims, that the butter knife was not actually missing.
  7. ↑ This item sometimes does not prompt a Perception check, for unknown reason.
  8. ↑ 8.0 8.1 Interacting with this item sometimes equips it to the corresponding slot of the controlled character's inventory. It is not known whether this behaviour is a bug.
  9. ↑ It may be necessary to pick up the item to trigger this commentary, rather than just interacting.
  10. ↑ The game asset used for the portrait item is a renamed version of the painting item "Portrait Of A Woman". Dialogue with  Wyll implies that this portrait is still accurate to what she looked like, albeit at a younger age.
  11. ↑ Worn by  Ch'r'ai Har'rak
  12. ↑ 12.0 12.1 Inside the Emperor's Wardrobe
  13. ↑ 13.0 13.1 Worn by W'wargaz, if he is present
  14. ↑ 14.0 14.1 Worn by Tska'an, if she is present
